text.p: Italy's debt market ended little changed on previous closing levels after the spread over 10-year benchmark bunds narrowed to 95 basis points and the September Btp Liffe contract set a new high at 136.40.

"The Italian market is still positive. But with Bunds at currently high levels and a dollar this strong our market is going to have to rise even more over Germany if it wants to make up more ground in terms of the spread," one trader said.
The September Btp ended just one basis point up at 136.25 while the Bund future eased seven bps to 102.75 after touching a 102.92 high. The Btp turned negative in APT trade.

"I reckon the market could be about to pause for a breather although I don't think the Btp will go below 135.80 where there's good support," one trader said. "For it to rise further we need good news on (Italian) welfare state reform," another said referring to continuing talks on the thorny question between government, unions and employers.

But another operator said, "if the spread continues to narrow I think the Btp contract, barring normal intraday downturns, could again touch new highs as soon as Wednesday." On the welfare state, he said there seemed to be signs of more willingness on all sides to reach an accord.
In cash bonds, the February 2007 Btp closing yield was 6.52 percent with the spread over the benchmark bund at 96 basis points.
"Everyone by now is betting the spread can go to 80 bps but it's clear that it won't all be played out at once and many operators are for the moment staying on the sidelines," one trader said.
On the interbank market, the overnight rate closed at an average 6.98 percent against a previous 6.99 percent with tomorrow/next at 6.99 percent from 7.0 percent.
